data.content:
## Implementation Plan — knots-edf8

Root cause: `persisted_machine_id` in src/machine.rs does read-check, then
plain `fs::write` on first use, silently discarding write errors. Two
racing processes on a fresh store (no /etc/machine-id, e.g. macOS) each
derive a different random-seeded id and both write; whichever write lands
last "wins" the file, but the loser still returns and USES its own
(different) derived value in memory, e.g. stamping a lease with an id that
never matches the persisted file again.

Fix (single file: src/machine.rs, plus threading a `Result` through ~9
existing call sites, no new files):

1. Atomic first-use persistence with convergence:
   - Write the candidate id to a uniquely-named temp file in the same
     directory (`.machine-id.tmp.<uuid>`), fully content-complete and
     fsynced.
   - `std::fs::hard_link(tmp, final_path)`: this is atomic create-if-absent
     on POSIX and Windows (fails with `AlreadyExists` iff another racer's
     hard_link already landed first). Using create_new directly on the
     final path was considered and rejected: a racer could observe the
     freshly-created empty file before the winner finishes writing it
     (a torn-read window). Writing to a fully-formed temp file first and
     only exposing it via hard_link removes that window.
   - On success, this process's derived value is the persisted value:
     return it directly.
   - On `AlreadyExists`, re-read the file and return ITS contents (the
     winner's value) instead of this process's own derived candidate, so
     every racer converges on the exact same string.
   - Always remove the temp file afterward (best-effort; the second
     directory entry from hard_link means removing it never touches the
     winning file's content).
   - An existing, non-empty file is read and returned without touching
     the file at all (unchanged fast path) — satisfies "existing stores
     keep their current machine id".

2. Surface persist errors instead of discarding them:
   - `machine_id`, `resolve_machine_id`, `persisted_machine_id` all change
     from `-> String` to `-> std::io::Result<String>`.
   - `App::machine_id()` becomes `-> Result<String, AppError>` (AppError
     already has an `Io` variant with `From<std::io::Error>`).
   - `ReplicationService`'s two direct callers (`src/replication.rs`,
     `src/sync/mod.rs`) already return `Result<_, SyncError>`, which also
     already has `Io(std::io::Error)` + `From`, so `?` threads through.
   - Update the ~9 call sites (src/lease.rs x2, src/app/state_fail_ops.rs,
     src/run_commands.rs, src/app/tests_list_lease.rs,
     src/replication/tests_lease_owner.rs x2) to propagate with `?` (all
     already inside functions returning a compatible `Result`) or
     `.expect(...)` in test helpers that return a bare value.

3. Document (not change) delete-and-regenerate behavior for acceptance
   criterion 3: on platforms with a real system machine id
   (`/etc/machine-id`), deleting `.knots/machine-id` regenerates the same
   id, because the seed is stable. On platforms with no system source
   (macOS/Windows with neither file present), the seed is a random UUID
   per call, so deleting the persisted file loses the identity and the
   next resolution mints and persists a new, unrelated id. This is
   documented explicitly in the module and function doc comments as a
   known, accepted trade-off — implementing a recoverable stable-seed
   scheme was explicitly a "Consider" (optional) bullet in the knot
   description, and the existing behavior only needs to be *defined and
   documented*, not changed, to satisfy the acceptance criterion. Keeping
   scope minimal here avoids inventing new persistent-seed machinery this
   knot doesn't require.

Tests (all in src/machine_tests.rs, extending the existing file):
- Concurrency test: spawn N (e.g. 16) OS threads calling
  `persisted_machine_id` on the same fresh store root simultaneously;
  assert all N results are equal and match the file's persisted contents.
- Existing-file test (already present as
  `persisted_machine_id_reuses_an_existing_file`) proves an existing file
  is never rewritten; extend/confirm mtime or content is untouched.
- Persist-failure-surfaces test: make the store root's parent
  unwritable/unreadable (or point at a path where the parent can't be
  created, e.g. through a file where a directory is expected) and assert
  `persisted_machine_id` returns `Err`, not a silently re-randomized
  value.
- Update existing tests for the new `Result` return type.

No new knots. No child knots. Single-commit change confined to
src/machine.rs, its test module, and threading the `Result` through the
small, enumerated set of existing callers above.
